speaker: Unknown
en: I think we are the product of the people that lift us up.
zh: 我认为我们是那些扶持我们的人的产物。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really believe that.
zh: 我真的这么相信。

speaker: Unknown
en: I never believe this bull crap.
zh: 我从不相信那些鬼话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, you know, I did this all myself.
zh: 哦,你知道的,这一切都是我自己做出来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who do you want behind you?
zh: 你想要谁在你身后?

speaker: Unknown
en: The one that believes in your mission or the one that you paid to be there, the mercenary?
zh: 是相信你使命的人,还是你付钱雇来的雇佣兵?

speaker: Unknown
en: You want the one who believes in your mission.
zh: 你想要相信你使命的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Try a startup while you're young.
zh: 趁年轻去尝试创业。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do you tell people that?
zh: 为什么你跟人们这么说?

speaker: Unknown
en: You learn a set of skills that is really hard to learn in a larger company because everybody's being so careful in a larger company.
zh: 你会学到一套在大公司里很难学到的技能,因为在大公司里每个人都太谨慎了。

speaker: Unknown
en: All that's stripped away in a startup.
zh: 而在创业公司里,这一切都被剥离掉了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're just trying to survive and you're trying to make it happen.
zh: 你只是在努力生存,努力把它变成现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is Masters of Scale.
zh: 这是 Masters of Scale。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Jeff Berman, your host.
zh: 我是 Jeff Berman,你的主持人。

speaker: Unknown
en: With us today is Andrew Anagnost, the CEO of Autodesk.
zh: 今天和我们在一起的是 Andrew Anagnost,Autodesk 的 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: And while you may not be familiar with the company itself, you're definitely familiar with the company does because pretty much everything that you are looking at in the real world, their software help make.
zh: 虽然你可能对这家公司本身并不熟悉,但你肯定对这家公司所做的事情很熟悉,因为你在现实世界中看到的一切,几乎都是用他们的软件帮助制造出来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome to Masters of Scale.
zh: 欢迎来到 Masters of Scale。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, we like to talk about Autodesk as the biggest tech company nobody's heard of.
zh: 是的,我们喜欢把 Autodesk 称作没人听说过的最大科技公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything that you see in the world, the cars that you see on the roads, the bridges they drive over, the machines that you see, the phone, the buildings, it's built and designed using our software.
zh: 你在世界上看到的一切,你在马路上看到的汽车、你开车经过的桥梁、你看到的机器、手机、建筑物,都是用我们的软件构建和设计的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm keen to get into the story of how you joined the company and became CEO and how you're leading it through this era.
zh: 我很想聊聊你是如何加入这家公司并成为 CEO 的故事,以及你是如何在这个时代领导它的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I want to go way back because we were learning before we started the recording that you and I have more than a few things in common.
zh: 但我想追溯得更早,因为我们在开始录音之前了解到,你和我有不少共同点。

speaker: Unknown
en: But one of them is neither of us was our best self as a teenager.
zh: 其中之一是,我们俩在青少年时期都不是最好的自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I was not my best self.
zh: 不,我不是最好的自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: What were your teen years like?
zh: 你的青少年时期是什么样的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, my teen years were a little rough, all right?
zh: 是的,我的青少年时期有点艰难,好吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: As I progressed through and got into high school, you know, I essentially started numbing myself.
zh: 随着我长大进入高中,你知道,我基本上开始麻醉自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: And lack of a better word, I self-medicated.
zh: 找个说法,我进行了自我麻醉。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just went off the rails and I dropped out of high school for a while there, ended up in the wrong places, was never a violent kid.
zh: 我彻底偏离了正轨,一度从高中辍学,出现在不该出现的地方,我从不是个暴力的小孩。

speaker: Unknown
en: The only person I really ever hurt was myself.
zh: 我真正伤害过的唯一一个人就是我自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, like I was the only high school dropout that would show up for like the, you know, the trigonometry class, sometimes under the influence of something.
zh: 你知道,比如我是唯一一个会去上三角函数课的高中辍学生,有时还在某种东西的影响下。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, one day one of the teachers came up to me and he said, you know what?
zh: 然后,你知道,有一天一位老师走到我面前,他说,你知道吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: You can ruin your life all you want, but you're not gonna ruin the rest of the people's lives in this room.
zh: 你可以随便毁掉你自己的生活,但你不能毁掉这个房间里其他人的生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: Get the hell out of my class.
zh: 给我滚出我的教室。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know?
zh: 你知道吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember to this day, right?
zh: 而我至今还记得,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: I can see his face in my face.
zh: 他的脸就在我面前。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can feel his breath, right?
zh: 我能感觉到他的呼吸,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, it's one of those things where at the moment I just laughed at him, didn't stick with me, but he was very brave, this teacher.
zh: 你知道,那一刻我只是嘲笑他,当时没往心里去,但这位老师非常勇敢。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember not that long later when I was expelled and I got into a very serious car accident, almost killed the passenger in the car.
zh: 我记得没过多久,我被开除后,遭遇了一场非常严重的车祸,差点害死了车上的乘客。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was handcuffed.
zh: 我被铐上了手铐。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was on the ground in a gravel driveway, you know, smashed down.
zh: 我趴在一个碎石车道上,你知道,被按倒在地。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was injured.
zh: 我受了伤。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, his voice just banged through my head.
zh: 然后,你知道,他的声音在我脑子里轰然响起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've never, I've never forgotten him.
zh: 我从来没有,我从来没有忘记过他。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mr. Carrington.
zh: Carrington 老师。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hello, Mr. Carrington, if you're still alive out there.
zh: 你好,Carrington 老师,如果您还在世的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most people that, you know, drop out of high school, get expelled, have problems, don't end up going to graduate school at Stanford.
zh: 大多数从高中辍学、被开除、有问题的人,最后不会去斯坦福读研究生。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in that respect, I'm kind of a statistical anomaly.
zh: 所以在这一点上,我算是一个统计学上的异类。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's because of people like that, actually, that I meant along the way that saw that I had potential and I was just pissing it away.
zh: 但这其实是因为这样的人,我在路上遇到的、看出我有潜力而我却在糟蹋它的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, Andrew, what happened between the face down, handcuffed in the gravel, having already had the experience with Mr. Carrington trying to get you back on the right track?
zh: 那么，Andrew，从脸朝下戴着 handcuffed 躺在碎石地上，还经历过 Carrington 先生试图把你拉回正轨之后，发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: That got you all the way to Stanford and that has us sitting here today?
zh: 是什么让你一路走到了 Stanford，又让我们今天坐在这里？

speaker: Unknown
en: That moment was pretty seminal in my life.
zh: 那个时刻在我的人生中是非常重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, having almost hurt someone, I think you just sit there and you reflect and go, what am I doing?
zh: 实际上，差点伤害到别人之后，我想你就是坐在那里反思，然后问自己：我到底在做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: It really was a switch moment.
zh: 那真的是一个转折时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was voices like that that kind of, you know, propelled me forward.
zh: 而且正是那些声音，你知道的，推动着我前进。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I got into the local Cal State.
zh: 你知道，我进了当地的 Cal State。

speaker: Unknown
en: I worked my way through that program.
zh: 我在那个项目中一路努力读完。

speaker: Unknown
en: I fought to get into internships.
zh: 我努力争取进入实习岗位。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had professors along the way that told me, look, you know, you...
zh: 我一路上有一些教授告诉我，听着，你知道，你……

speaker: Unknown
en: You have potential, you know, they believed in me, you know, and I believe that you have to work hard.
zh: 你有潜力，你知道，他们相信我，你知道，而我相信你必须努力工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: You do make your own luck in some ways, but you know, it's kind of a fool's errand to think that your environment hasn't in some way either pulled you down or pushed you up.
zh: 在某种程度上你确实能创造自己的运气，但你知道，认为环境没有在某种程度上拉低你或推高你，那有点像傻瓜的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was fortunate that some of these people really believed in me and I was not gonna let them down.
zh: 而我很幸运，这些人中有些真的相信我，而我不打算让他们失望。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's something really profound about the there but for the grace of God of this.
zh: 这件事里“若非上帝恩典，那人就是我”的部分确实非常深刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: How incredible that you had people who stepped in for you and helped you get on track.
zh: 你有那些挺身而出帮你、帮你走上正轨的人，这多么不可思议。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did, including the judge that chewed me out in juvenile court.
zh: 我确实有，包括那个在少年法庭把我狠狠训了一顿的法官。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, look, I think we are the product of the people that lift us up.
zh: 你知道，听着，我认为我们是被那些托举我们的人塑造的产物。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really believe that.
zh: 我真的相信这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: My life experience has taught me that.
zh: 我的人生经历教会了我这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I never believe this bull crap that I hear out there about, oh, you know, I did this all myself.
zh: 我从不相信我外面听到的那些胡扯，什么，哦，你知道，这一切都是我自己做到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: For the most important people in your life, they tell you what you need to hear, not what you want to hear.
zh: 对于你生命中最重要的那些人来说，他们告诉你的是你需要听的，而不是你想听的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you get through this, you get to Stanford, you get your PhD, you don't go into academia.
zh: 于是你度过了这一切，你进了 Stanford，你拿到 PhD，你没有进入学术界。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I don't.
zh: 是的，我没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you end up at Autodesk?
zh: 你最后是怎么去 Autodesk 的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I actually went to a startup.
zh: 其实我去了初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a deep technology startup in Boston and spent almost five years at a startup, which was a magical experience, all right?
zh: 那是 Boston 的一家深科技初创公司，我在那家初创公司待了将近五年，那是一段奇妙的经历，好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I tell young people, you should try a startup while you're young.
zh: 我是说，我告诉年轻人，趁年轻时你应该试试初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do you tell people that?
zh: 你为什么这样告诉别人？

speaker: Unknown
en: When you're at a startup, what you do is you learn a little of everything very quickly.
zh: 当你在一家初创公司时，你做的就是很快地学到一点方方面面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a startup is very low hierarchy.
zh: 而且初创公司的层级非常低。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if there is any hierarchy, most people ignore it.
zh: 即使有任何层级，大多数人也会无视它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you make decisions very quickly.
zh: 而且你做决定非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: You learn the value of speed and arguing things out in kind of a Socratic way where the ideas got to be challenged, not the people.
zh: 你学会速度的价值，以及用一种苏格拉底式的方式把事情争论清楚，即挑战的是想法，而不是人。

speaker: Unknown
en: You learn a set of skills that is really hard to learn in a larger company because everybody's being so careful in a larger company or they're being so political or all these things, all that's stripped away in a startup.
zh: 你学到一套在更大公司里真的很难学到的技能，因为在大公司里每个人都那么小心，或者那么讲政治，或者诸如此类，而这一切在初创公司里都被剥离掉了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're just trying to survive and you're trying to make it happen.
zh: 你只是在努力生存，你在努力把它做成。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that journey from zero to $10 million is so educational.
zh: 所以从零到 1000 万美元的那段旅程非常有教育意义。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: And from zero to 30, 50 people or so, you kind of know everything happening in the company.
zh: 而从零到 30、50 人左右，你几乎知道公司里发生的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know everything.
zh: 你知道一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody knows everything.
zh: 每个人都知道一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you know exactly who to go to to get something done.
zh: 而且你确切知道该找谁把事情办成。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you know how to get your relationships in place.
zh: 而且你知道如何把你的关系建立到位。

speaker: Unknown
en: You also know that you can cut through the BS.
zh: 你也知道你能cut through那些 BS。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, of course, it teaches you some things that do not translate to large company environments.
zh: 当然，它教会你的一些东西是无法迁移到大公司环境的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This high speed connection that you have in a startup where, you know, you've been sitting there late at night eating with these people and you can call BS on them and they don't feel bad doesn't translate.
zh: 这种你在初创公司里拥有的高速连接——你知道，你曾和这些人深夜坐在一起吃饭，你可以对他们说 BS，而他们不会觉得难受——是无法迁移的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I was actually recruited out of this company by Autodesk.
zh: 所以我实际上是被 Autodesk 从这家公司挖走的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the funny thing was, is I, I meant the woman who would become my wife and she wanted to move to California.
zh: 但有趣的是，我，我遇到了后来成为我妻子的那个女人，而她想搬到 California。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, wow.
zh: 哦，哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were working for competing software companies.
zh: 我们当时在为相互竞争的软件公司工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you believe that?
zh: 你能相信吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow.
zh: 哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The only reason I took the job though is because it was in a team that was trying to fight against this company that I had actually partnered with at my startup.
zh: 不过我接下这份工作的唯一原因是,它所在团队的使命是对抗一家公司,而我在创业时曾和那家公司合作过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I go, oh yeah, they're terrible.
zh: 我就想,哦对,他们太糟糕了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We should build a product that defeats them.
zh: 我们应该打造一个击败他们的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I got a little bit excited about that, but let's face it.
zh: 所以我对此有点兴奋,但说实话,

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought it was a stepping stone to something else.
zh: 我当时以为这只是一个通往别处的跳板。

speaker: Unknown
en: It turns out that, you know, when I got there, I really liked being in this counterculture team that I was working with.
zh: 结果发现,我到了那里之后,真的很喜欢和我共事的这个反主流文化的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: A rebellious team in terms of rebelling against the primary culture in the company.
zh: 一个反叛的团队,反叛的是公司里的主流文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: How big was Autodesk at the time?
zh: 当时的 Autodesk 有多大规模?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, less than a thousand employees.
zh: 应该说,不到一千名员工。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, but still not an early stage startup.
zh: 好的,但仍然不是早期初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not an early stage startup.
zh: 不是早期初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Relatively scale.
zh: 相对有规模了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Big enough to have a well-established culture and well-established norms.
zh: 大到已经拥有成熟的文化和成熟的规范。

speaker: Unknown
en: And most companies at that scale with well-established culture and norms, they may say they want a rebel group, they may say they want the innovator, but generally it doesn't go so well.
zh: 而大多数达到那种规模、拥有成熟文化和规范的公司,他们可能会说自己想要一个反叛小组,可能会说自己想要创新者,但通常结局不会太好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Carol Bartz did this, okay?
zh: Carol Bartz 就是这么做的,好吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Carol Bartz set up this team.
zh: 是 Carol Bartz 设立了这个团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were butting up against the big established part of the company that was really built on top of the poor product that the company started with, which was called AutoCAD, the name that most people know.
zh: 我们在和公司里那个庞大的成熟部门硬碰硬,那个部门完全建立在公司起家的那款糟糕产品之上,也就是大多数人都知道的那个名字——AutoCAD。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was kind of an exciting period.
zh: 那是一段挺激动人心的时期。

speaker: Unknown
en: I learned a lot about how you operate and how you kind of use the edge but then soften the edge over time through that experience.
zh: 通过那段经历,我学到了很多关于如何运作、如何利用边缘、然后随着时间推移把边缘磨软的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Carol Bartz, she kind of showed me the importance of...
zh: Carol Bartz,她让我明白了……的重要性,

speaker: Unknown
en: Commercial discipline and the rigor associated with that and the need to have accountability on getting things to customers in order to scale.
zh: 商业纪律以及与之相关的严谨,还有在规模化过程中对把东西交付给客户这件事要有问责。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I knew zero to 10 pretty well.
zh: 因为我对从零到十了解得很透彻。

speaker: Unknown
en: 10 to 100, you know, I didn't know that very well, right?
zh: 但从十到一百,你知道的,我不太了解,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: She was really influential on me and I look back at her in positive ways.
zh: 她对我影响真的很大,我回顾她时是带着正面评价的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I always like to say, I'm the product of two dysfunctional parents and they both have initials CB.
zh: 我总喜欢说,我是两个失职父母的孩子,而他们的首字母缩写都是 CB。

speaker: Unknown
en: One was Carol Bartz, one was Carl Bass.
zh: 一个是 Carol Bartz,一个是 Carl Bass。

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally different people, okay?
zh: 完全不同的两个人,好吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Both CEOs that I reported to.
zh: 都是我汇报过的 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: Carol much more on the commercial side.
zh: Carol 更多是在商业这一边。

speaker: Unknown
en: Carl on the, you know, respect for innovation, you know, respect for the customers' processes and what they do.
zh: Carl 则是在,你知道的,尊重创新,尊重客户的流程以及他们所做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Each of them taught me something.
zh: 他们每个人都教了我一些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Each of them taught me what to do and what not to do in many ways.
zh: 他们每个人都教了我该做什么、不该做什么,在很多方面都是。

speaker: Unknown
en: What did Carol and Carl do to allow a rebellious group inside the company not just to function but to flourish?
zh: Carol 和 Carl 做了什么,才让公司内部的一个反叛小组不仅能够运转,还能蓬勃发展?

speaker: Unknown
en: Carol only allowed a small number of these, like one.
zh: Carol 只允许少数几个这样的小组存在,比如就一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: She had a good sense for who could push things and who could not, and she supported them.
zh: 她对谁能推动事情、谁不能很有判断力,而且她会支持他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Carl, on the other hand, would create hundreds of these.
zh: 而 Carl 恰恰相反,他会创造出几百个这样的小组。

speaker: Unknown
en: He'd let them pop up everywhere to the point that it would stress the company's ability to execute.
zh: 他任由它们到处冒出来,以至于会压垮公司的执行能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Carl's style was much more let a thousand flowers bloom and maybe never prune a single flower.
zh: Carl 的风格更像是让千花齐放,而且可能从来不修剪任何一朵花。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's almost like working at two different companies with leaders that different.
zh: 在领导风格如此不同的两家公司工作,简直就像在两个完全不同的公司工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 绝对是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Very different companies.
zh: 非常不同的两家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even the company that I run now is Autodesk.
zh: 连我现在经营的这家公司 Autodesk,

speaker: Unknown
en: It's somewhat different, but it learned from both of those companies.
zh: 也有点不同,但它从那两家公司身上都学到了东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'd like to think that because we can scale new businesses, because we're very passionate about killing our own businesses, killing our own products, which we are very passionate, and I think that's a cultural norm in the company, that I've done a decent job, but I owe it to the experience and the experience arc.
zh: 而且我愿意相信,因为我们能够规模化新业务,因为我们非常热衷于杀死自己的业务、杀死自己的产品——我们对此非常热衷,我认为这是公司里的一种文化规范——我做得还算不错,但这要归功于那段经历和那段经历的弧线。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to come back to the norm of killing your own businesses when you need to, but I do want to hear about the journey to CEO because you weren't given the job outright.
zh: 我想回头再聊「在需要时杀死自己业务」这个规范,但我确实想听听你走向 CEO 的历程,因为这个职位并不是直接给你的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You had to really fight for it.
zh: 你必须真的为之拼搏。

speaker: Unknown
en: Will you tell us about the process that started as a co-CEO and led to the lone CEO?
zh: 你能给我们讲讲从联席 CEO 开始、最终走向独立 CEO 的那个过程吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: When they started the succession planning before the activists came into the company that ultimately led to the co-CEO scenario, I opted myself out of the succession process.
zh: 当他们在激进投资者进入公司之前开始继任规划时——那个规划最终促成了联席 CEO 的局面——我自己主动退出了继任流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I just never saw myself that way.
zh: 因为我从来没把自己往那方面想。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, for some reason, I looked at that job and I said, well, then you don't have any fun anymore, which might actually be true.
zh: 你知道，出于某种原因，我看着那份工作说：好，那你就再也没有乐趣了——这也许其实是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was only as the activist process progressed, okay, there was someone from the old culture that was up.
zh: 直到激进投资者的流程推进下去，好吧，有一位旧文化的代表在竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was me, you know, from the newer culture, the inside outsider.
zh: 还有我，你知道，来自较新文化的那个「内部的外来者」。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there was the threat of an outsider.
zh: 然后还有外来者带来的威胁。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as I was looking at the plot evolving, the culture norm wasn't going to get the job.
zh: 当我看着这个局面的演变，那个代表文化常态的人不会得到这份工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was very clear to anyone that that wasn't going to happen.
zh: 任何人都很清楚那不会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And more and more, I just said, okay, that means an outsider.
zh: 而且越来越多地，我只是说：好吧，那就意味着是一个外来者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love this company.
zh: 我热爱这家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's when I said...
zh: 那就是我说……

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm putting my name in.
zh: 我要报名了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to try for this job.
zh: 我想争取这个职位。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's how I ended up in this situation where they then pitted the old timer against me in the co-CEO role.
zh: 就是这样我最后落到了这个境地，然后他们把那位老将和我放进了联席 CEO 的角色里对决。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for six months, no decisions were made at the company.
zh: 而且六个月里，公司没有任何决策被做出。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why did they do that?
zh: 他们为什么要那样做？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's not exactly a model that's likely to work unless you are deeply partnered.
zh: 我是说，这并不是一个很可能会奏效的模式，除非你们深度合伙。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unless you're, it works much better at smaller companies than it would ever work at a large company, right?
zh: 除非你们——它在小公司里行得通的程度远胜于在大公司里，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they did it because they were afraid of disrupting the current culture of the company.
zh: 我认为他们那样做是因为害怕打乱公司当前的文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they were creating theater, all right, about, you know, we got to make sure that we assess all.
zh: 我认为他们是在制造戏剧，好吧，就是关于，你知道，我们得确保我们评估了所有（人选）。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were buying themselves time, all right, to get through the process.
zh: 他们是在给自己争取时间，好吧，好撑过这个流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was awkward for both of us, all right, and it wasn't a great time.
zh: 而且这对我们俩来说都很别扭，好吧，那不是一段好时光。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I said, for six months, no major strategic decisions were made at the company.
zh: 就像我说的，六个月里，公司没有任何重大战略决策被做出。

speaker: Unknown
en: And were daggers out?
zh: 那么当时有没有刀光剑影？

speaker: Unknown
en: Were you all basically trying to kill each other?
zh: 你们基本上是不是在互相置对方于死地？

speaker: Unknown
en: What was the dynamic?
zh: 那时的动态是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, no, we weren't like that.
zh: 不，不，我们不是那样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, at least, you know, I could speak for myself.
zh: 我是说，至少，你知道，我只能代表我自己说话。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wasn't like that.
zh: 我不是那样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I knew intuitively that the job was probably going to go to me, not necessarily because I was more deserving, you know, or all of those things, but because I was the inside outsider.
zh: 我凭直觉知道这份工作很可能会落到我头上，不一定是因为我更配得上，你知道，或诸如此类的原因，而是因为我是那个「内部的外来者」。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's what people wanted at that point.
zh: 而且我认为那就是当时人们想要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And frankly, it's probably what the company needed.
zh: 坦率地说，那大概也是公司所需要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They needed a separation from the Carl era.
zh: 他们需要与 Carl 时代做一个切割。

speaker: Unknown
en: They needed to move forward.
zh: 他们需要向前走。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think they wanted to do it in as gentle a way as they possibly could and make it look, make it visibly look like it was a fair process.
zh: 而且我认为他们想用尽可能温和的方式去做，并让它看起来，让它表面上看起来像是一个公平的流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to ask them, right?
zh: 你得去问他们，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: But it wasn't great.
zh: 但那并不好受。

speaker: Unknown
en: It wasn't a fun time.
zh: 那不是一段愉快的时光。

zh: 当你通过自己的事业积累了可观的财富时，它往往被绑定在单一股权头寸上。

en: The upside is real, but so is the risk, and knowing when to act isn't always obvious.
zh: 上行空间是真实的，但风险也是，而知道何时行动并不总是显而易见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Creative Planning, where wealth works together.
zh: Creative Planning，让财富协同运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learn more at creativeplanning.com slash masters of scale.
zh: 请访问 creativeplanning.com/scale 了解更多。

zh: 在我们进入今天对话的其余部分之前，我想花一点时间向你介绍 Masters of Scale Summit，它将于今年 10 月 20 日至 22 日重返旧金山。

en: So many of us feel overwhelmed right now.
zh: 我们很多人此刻都感到不堪重负。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like so much of the world is careening and we don't have power.
zh: 感觉世界的大部分都在失控疾驰，而我们没有力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't have agency.
zh: 我们没有主观能动性。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the thing about the Masters of Scale Summit.
zh: 这就是 Masters of Scale Summit 的意义所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really designed to remind us that we do have agency.
zh: 它真正是要提醒我们,我们确实拥有主观能动性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Agency to lead, agency to design, to build the relationships and the partnerships that empower us and to make the change that we want to see.
zh: 去引领的主观能动性,去设计、去建立赋能我们的关系和伙伴关系、去做出我们想看到的改变的主观能动性。

speaker: Unknown
en: We program a stage, we curate an audience, we set a schedule that builds in time for these relationships to be made and to grow so that by the time you leave Summit, you are fired out of a cannon, ready to run through walls to do better in the world with the agency that you actually have.
zh: 我们设计舞台,我们策划听众,我们制定一个日程表,为这些关系的建立和成长留出时间,这样等你离开 Summit 时,你就像从大炮里发射出去一样,准备好用你实际拥有的主观能动性去撞穿墙壁,把这个世界做得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope to see you there.
zh: 我希望在那里见到你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Visit mastersofscale.com slash summit.
zh: 访问 mastersofscale.com 斜杠 summit。

en: Humans will never be more intelligent than AI.
zh: 人类永远不会比 AI 更聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's going to be two types of companies.
zh: 将会有两类公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are great at AI and those that went out of business because they weren't.
zh: 一类擅长 AI,另一类因为不擅长而倒闭了。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we build a future that is human-centered?
zh: 我们如何构建一个以人为本的未来?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Rana Elkayubi, and on my podcast, Pioneers of AI, we answer that question and so many more.
zh: 我是 Rana Elkayubi,在我的播客 Pioneers of AI 上,我们回答这个问题以及更多问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: As an AI scientist, entrepreneur, and investor, I know what it takes to build AI that works for everyone.
zh: 作为一名 AI 科学家、创业者和投资人,我知道打造对每个人都有效的 AI 需要什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every week, I sit down with the pioneers shaping our future, and we take you behind the scenes of the AI that's transforming our lives.
zh: 每周,我会与塑造我们未来的先驱者坐下来,带你走进正在改变我们生活的 AI 的幕后。

speaker: Unknown
en: Find Pioneers of AI wherever you tune in.
zh: 在你收听播客的任何地方找到 Pioneers of AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you became the sole CEO, what was job one day one?
zh: 当你成为唯一的 CEO 时,第一天的第一项工作是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I fundamentally believe that you've got to have a guess at what the future is, okay?
zh: 我从根本上相信,你必须对未来有一个猜测,好吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: You've got to have a guess.
zh: 你必须有一个猜测。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you have to have the fortitude and the strength to pay attention when your guess is wrong and correct.
zh: 然后你必须有毅力和力量,当你的猜测错了时去注意并纠正。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I pulled out a lot of flowers that I thought were weeds.
zh: 所以我拔掉了很多我以为杂草的花。

speaker: Unknown
en: A couple of real flowers got pulled out in the process, and I had to dig out of that over time.
zh: 在这个过程中有几朵真正的花被拔掉了,我不得不在之后的时间里慢慢弥补。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was move number one.
zh: 那是我的第一步棋。

speaker: Unknown
en: And believe it or not, I shifted money to the back office, which is a very odd thing to do.
zh: 而且信不信由你,我把钱转移到了后端办公室,这是一件很奇怪的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow, yeah.
zh: 哇,是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right?
zh: 好吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: And here's the reason why I did it, because you might not know, but I was the one that led the subscription transition at Autodesk and started fixing the back office and trying to get it in a position where it can scale in an era where we have SaaS products.
zh: 我这么做的原因是,你可能不知道,我正是在 Autodesk 主导订阅转型的人,开始修复后端办公室,努力让它在一个我们有 SaaS 产品的时代里能够规模化地站稳脚跟。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that was the first thing I did.
zh: 但那是我做的第一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: When it sounds like, Andrew, what you saw was you had a foundation that wouldn't support the skyscraper you were trying to build.
zh: 听起来,Andrew,你所看到的是,你有一个无法支撑你想建的摩天大楼的地基。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could build the best products in the world right now, and I couldn't get it out to the customer.
zh: 我现在可以造出世界上最好的产品,但我没办法把它交付给客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I certainly couldn't get it to new customers.
zh: 我当然也没办法把它交付给新客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: The next thing I did was I made a couple of large acquisitions for Autodesk to scale the construction business because
zh: 我接下来做的事是为 Autodesk 做了几笔大型收购,以扩大建筑业务,因为

speaker: Unknown
en: I believe firmly that in the world of hyper-automation that we were heading into, just being a design software company, which is what we were back then, wasn't gonna be enough.
zh: 我坚信,在我们正在迈入的超自动化时代,仅仅做一家设计软件公司——也就是我们当时的样子——是不够的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had to be a design and make software company.
zh: 我们必须成为一家设计和制造软件公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had to extend ourselves across the process.
zh: 我们必须把自己延伸到整个流程之中。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I went big on trying to do that.
zh: 所以我在努力做到这一点上下了大注。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was the next thing I did as I kind of progressed through my early days as a CEO.
zh: 那是我作为 CEO 早期推进过程中做的下一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was quite successful.
zh: 而且那是相当成功的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We scaled the business.
zh: 我们把业务扩大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was hard.
zh: 很艰难。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had to overspend, but we scaled it.
zh: 我们不得不超支,但我们把它扩大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you have the right team or did you also have to overhaul your leadership team?
zh: 你的团队是对的吗,还是你也必须重组你的领导团队?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think three quarters of the leadership team either, you know, left on their own or were asked to leave.
zh: 我认为领导团队有四分之三的人要么,你知道,自己离开,要么被要求离开。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a lot of change for a big, for a skilled company.
zh: 对于一家大型、一家有实力的公司来说,这是很大的变动。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a lot of, it was a lot of change.
zh: 这是非常,非常大的变动。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some of these were good people.
zh: 而且其中一些人是好人。 [[239-补充]] 他们只是不适合我正在尝试做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: They just weren't the right fit for what I was trying to do.
zh: 它们只是不适合我想要做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you manage the communication to the rest of the team as they're seeing this changeover at the top of the company that, no, no, no, this is actually good.
zh: 当团队其他人看到公司高层发生这种换血时,你是如何管理沟通的,让他们明白,不,不,不,这其实是好事。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is where we're going.
zh: 这就是我们要去的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I over-communicated about it a lot.
zh: 是的,我在这件事上进行了大量的过度沟通。

speaker: Unknown
en: I spent a lot of time saying why.
zh: 我花了很多时间解释为什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I told the why story over and over again.
zh: 我一遍又一遍地讲那个「为什么」的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I gave elements of the what and left some of the what to everybody else to kind of like challenge, right?
zh: 然后我给出了「做什么」的一些要素,并把「做什么」的一部分留给大家去质疑,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And engage with, but I spent a lot of time talking about the why to the company.
zh: 并且参与其中,但我花了很多时间向公司讲述这个「为什么」。

speaker: Unknown
en: And let's face it, I had to build trust because in a company like this,
zh: → 修正:[[261]] 我会陪你一起扯。

speaker: Unknown
en: Half were for me, half were for the other guy.
zh: 一半人支持我,一半人支持另一个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sure.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: Was it exactly 50-50?
zh: 正好是一半对一半吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, who knows?
zh: 哦,谁知道呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's pretty close.
zh: 差不多很接近。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I had to earn not only the trust of the other half, but I had to prove myself to the half that was for me, that, you know, were you the right person?
zh: 所以我不仅要赢得另一半人的信任,我还必须向支持我的那一半证明自己——你到底是不是对的人?

speaker: Unknown
en: So I had to be a whole company leader.
zh: 所以我必须成为一个面向整个公司的领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that, unlike some of the leadership we have today, but I won't digress down these avenues, I had to be a whole company leader.
zh: → 修正:[[265]] 你所做的只是燃烧卡路里,浪费精力,浪费金钱,浪费时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're welcome to digress anywhere you wanna go.
zh: 你想在哪儿扯远都可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll go there with you.
zh: 我会和你一起去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, you know what?
zh: 嗯,你知道吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if you really wanna be effective, you have to prevent thrashing.
zh: 我觉得如果你真想高效,你必须防止来回摇摆。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you pander to one extreme or the other in a company, in a society or anything, you thrash and you thrash back and forth and you have this illusion of progress, but you don't.
zh: 当你在公司、社会或任何事情上迎合某一个极端时,你就会来回摇摆、反复折腾,你会有一种进步的错觉,但其实没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: What you're doing is you're burning calories, wasting energy, wasting money and wasting time.
zh: 你这么做的结果是在燃烧卡路里,浪费精力,浪费金钱,浪费时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I had to make sure that I didn't thrash the company.
zh: 所以我必须确保不让公司来回摇摆。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I worked hard to win over the people that saw some of their darlings depart
zh: 所以我努力去争取那些眼睁睁看着自己的心头项目被砍掉的人,

speaker: Unknown
en: And I worked hard to bring some of the people that were with me over into the other side.
zh: 我也努力把一些原本站在我这边的人带到另一边去。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I cross-pollinated a little bit and I didn't punish people for what side of the fence they stood on.
zh: 所以我做了一点交叉融合,我没有因为人们站在栅栏的哪一边而惩罚他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I had earned trust, let's be very clear here.
zh: 但要明确一点:我确实赢得了信任。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I didn't have much time to do it.
zh: 而且我没有太多时间去做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, you have to earn that trust in like the first one or two years because when you're asking the company to sacrifice, especially when you do a big riff of like darling projects, you know, and just send them off, people aren't, you know, they're not your fans right at this point, they're questioning you.
zh: 你知道,你必须在大约头一两年里赢得那种信任,因为当你要求公司做出牺牲时,尤其是当你大刀阔斧砍掉一批心头项目、直接送走它们的时候,人们在那一刻并不是你的粉丝,他们在质疑你。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was hard work telling the company the why over and over again and then actually delivering some success.
zh: 所以,一遍又一遍地向公司讲述「为什么」,然后真正交付一些成功,这是一件很辛苦的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to just drill in also to this decision to kill businesses, to pluck weeds that may actually have been flowers.
zh: 我还想深入探讨一下这个砍掉业务的决策,去拔掉那些实际上可能是花朵的杂草。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I can imagine there are some people who are like, awesome, finally, like we're making these decisions, whatever.
zh: 因为我可以想象,有些人会觉得,太棒了,终于,我们终于在做这些决定了,之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I have to bet there are a lot of people are like, but wait, that's my baby.
zh: 但我敢打赌,肯定有很多人的想法是,可是等等,那是我的心血。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're killing innovation.
zh: 你在扼杀创新。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I guess two parts.
zh: 所以我想分两部分来说。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, what was your process for making that decision?
zh: 第一,你做那个决定时的流程是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And then how did you manage the human emotion behind the attachment to some of the projects you're killing?
zh: 然后第二,你如何管理人们对那些被你砍掉的项目所产生的情感依恋?

speaker: Unknown
en: The process had a few simple tests, okay?
zh: 那个流程有几个简单的测试,好吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a big believer in a few simple rules set you free.
zh: 我非常信奉一点:几条简单的规则能让你获得自由。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the tests were this, do we have a right to win?
zh: 这些测试是这样的:我们有没有获胜的权利?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there something special about Autodesk, the markets we serve, or what we do that gives us some kind of right to win?
zh: Autodesk 有没有什么特别之处,我们所服务的市场或者我们所做的事情,能给我们某种获胜的权利?

speaker: Unknown
en: The other thing I ask is, how adjacent is it to our current business or how far away is it?
zh: 另一个我要问的是,它与我们现在的主营业务有多邻近,或者有多远?

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the distance from our business?
zh: 它距离我们的业务有多远?

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, the reason I asked that question is because the further something is away from your business, the harder it is for you to get to it over a period of time.
zh: 我问这个问题的原因是,一件事离你的业务越远,随着时间推移,你就越难做到它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because usually what you wanna do is do hops, but if you take a big leap, sometimes you leap too far.
zh: 因为通常你想做的是小步跨越,但如果你来一次大跳跃,有时候你会跳得太远。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how close is the adjacency was the other test.
zh: 所以,邻近程度有多近,是另一个测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the third one was, do I have the team?
zh: 然后第三个是,我有没有那个团队?

speaker: Unknown
en: Do I have the right product vision and the things associated with that?
zh: 我有没有正确的产品愿景以及与之相关的东西?

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, a bunch of things quickly were like, nope, nope, nope, nope.
zh: 然后,有一堆事情很快就变成了,不行,不行,不行,不行。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of them, two of them, I got wrong and, you know, I live with that.
zh: 其中有一两个,我判断错了,你知道,我接受这个结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: I still make a joke out of it because I'm still digging out of the hole.
zh: 我现在还拿这个开玩笑,因为我还在从那个坑里往外爬。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're right, 70% of the time you're killing it, okay?
zh: 如果你 70% 的时候是对的,你就已经干得非常出色了,好吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: You're just killing it.
zh: 你就是干得非常出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's the process I took to decide what stays and what goes.
zh: 这就是我决定去留取舍所经历的流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: The hop versus leap is one exception if you think your entire business is about to hit a wall.
zh: 小跳与飞跃是个例外——如果你认为你的整个业务即将撞墙。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, just think about the Netflix transition as an example, which, okay, it's illogical, but that was more of a leap than a hop.
zh: 比如，就以 Netflix 的转型为例，好吧，这有点不合逻辑，但那更像是飞跃而不是小跳。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was a leap.
zh: 那是一次飞跃。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean- Yeah.
zh: 我是说——是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when we went to subscription, that was a leap.
zh: 所以当我们转向订阅制时，那是一次飞跃。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: The hop philosophy makes a ton of sense.
zh: 小跳的理念非常有道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: When do you have to take the leap?
zh: 那什么时候你必须去飞跃呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, when there's paradigm shifts, okay?
zh: 是的，当出现范式转变的时候，好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's differences between leaping into a new technology, which I think you have to do when your business is threatened, and leaping into a completely new market where even an acquisition might stress the organization beyond where it is.
zh: 所以，飞跃进入一项新技术，我认为当你的业务受到威胁时你必须这么做；而飞跃进入一个全新的市场，即使是一次收购也可能把组织压得超出它的承受范围，这两者是有区别的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we leap into technologies at Autodesk, we hop into adjacencies.
zh: 所以在 Autodesk,我们对技术是飞跃，对邻近领域是小跳。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so far, so good, all right?
zh: 到目前为止，一切顺利，好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: We were on AI quite early.
zh: 我们很早就投入了 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we leap into the technology,
zh: 所以我们对技术是飞跃，

speaker: Unknown
en: Trying not to be too early, you know the balance, right?
zh: 尽量不要太早，你懂这个平衡的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Too early, you spend too much money, too late, and you spend too much money and have no success.
zh: 太早，你会花太多钱；太晚，你也会花太多钱，而且毫无成果。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where are you in your AI transformation and where do you see it going?
zh: 你们的 AI 转型进行到哪一步了，你觉得它会走向何方？

speaker: Unknown
en: First off, let's talk about why it's so important, okay?
zh: 首先，我们谈谈为什么这件事如此重要，好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a massive capacity problem in the built world.
zh: 在建筑建造领域，我们有一个巨大的产能问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the civil building and construction world, we need to build a lot.
zh: 在土木建筑和施工领域，我们需要建造大量的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We all know the housing problems in California.
zh: 我们都知道加州的住房问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: We all understand it's not just a technology problem at all.
zh: 我们都明白，这完全不仅仅是一个技术问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an ecosystem problem, but technology can help the ecosystem because one thing that's really-
zh: 这是一个生态系统问题，但技术可以帮助这个生态系统，因为——

speaker: Unknown
en: broken about how you build civil infrastructure, buildings and homes, is it's this fragmented ecosystem with highly competing people that like to sue each other and no traceability or accountability, nothing any manufacturer would ever accept.
zh: 建造土木基础设施、楼宇和房屋的方式中，非常破碎的一点在于：这是一个碎片化的生态系统，充斥着高度互相竞争、动辄互相起诉的人群，没有任何可追溯性或问责机制，任何制造商都绝不会接受这种状况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now on manufacturing, which we're also in,
zh: 现在说制造业，我们也身处其中，

speaker: Unknown
en: Highly automated factories of the future.
zh: 高度自动化的未来工厂。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the only way the U.S. is gonna be competitive in building things in U.S. soil.
zh: 这是美国要在美国本土造东西还能保持竞争力的唯一途径。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have to move to super automation there.
zh: 所以在那里你必须转向超级自动化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd like to bring some of this discipline of transparency from manufacturing to the building world.
zh: 我想把制造业的这种透明度纪律带到建筑建造领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I just wanted to characterize the capacity problem we have in the industry.
zh: 所以我只是想描述一下我们这个行业所面临的产能问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So where are we on our AI journey?
zh: 那么，我们在 AI 之旅上走到哪里了？

speaker: Unknown
en: We have been working really hard to automate the design process and converge it with the making process, either construction or manufacturing.
zh: 我们一直在非常努力地自动化设计流程，并使其与制造流程——无论是施工还是制造——融合趋同。

speaker: Unknown
en: So use AI as kind of project intelligence or a brain in the middle that kind of helps you make decisions about design that are informed by what it takes to construct or manufacture something or make decisions about construction or manufacturing that inform the design and connect those things and automate them as much as you possibly can.
zh: 也就是把 AI 当作某种项目智能，或者说一个处于中间的大脑，帮助你做出关于设计的决策，而这些决策是由建造或制造某样东西所需的条件来支撑的；或者做出关于施工或制造的决策，反过来支撑设计；并把这些东西连接起来，尽可能地自动化。

speaker: Unknown
en: This has been something that we've been working through for eight, nine years.
zh: 这件事我们已经做了八、九年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We call it convergence, the convergence of design and make, the convergence of construction and manufacturing, convergence of digital and physical worlds.
zh: 我们称之为融合(design and make 的融合)，设计与制造的融合，施工与制造的融合，数字世界与物理世界的融合。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is what we call it internally.
zh: 这是我们内部的叫法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd say on our journey, we've made huge progress.
zh: 我想说，在这段旅程中，我们取得了巨大的进展。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've got AI under everything.
zh: 我们把 AI 放进了所有东西的底层。

speaker: Unknown
en: We built our own custom AI models off of data that we have from our customers, controversial with our customers.
zh: 我们基于从客户那里获得的数据构建了自己的定制 AI 模型，这在客户中是有争议的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're super transparent with our customers, though, about what we're doing.
zh: 不过，我们对客户在这一点上是非常透明的，我们会说明我们在做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is it controversial with your customers?
zh: 为什么这在客户中有争议呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, because are you training other people on my IP to do what I do in my special sauce?
zh: 呃，因为——你是不是在用我的 IP 训练别人，让他们去做我做的事，复制我的独门秘方？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we tell people is this, if we do that, you're gonna be able to opt out of that training.
zh: 而我们告诉大家的是这样：如果我们那么做，你将可以选择退出那种训练。

speaker: Unknown
en: We will erase your data from that training set.
zh: 我们会把你的数据从那个训练集中抹除。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's not what we're doing right now.
zh: 但那不是我们现在正在做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we're doing is we're training for productivity.
zh: 我们现在做的是为了生产力而训练。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're doing it by using the data to train our own custom models that are high speed, high performance.
zh: 我们的做法是利用数据来训练我们自己的定制模型，做到高速、高性能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also using the context of what they're doing to actually help them get better answers.
zh: 同时也利用他们正在做的事情的上下文，来真正帮助他们获得更好的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you know, everybody says, well, aren't the large language models going to replace that world?
zh: 你知道，每个人都会说，大语言模型不是要取代那个世界吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a couple of things that we all have to pay attention to here.
zh: 我认为这里有几件事我们大家都必须注意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably right is wrong in our business.
zh: 在我们的行业里，大概对就是错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably right ends up with machines that don't work.
zh: 大概对最终会得到不能用的机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's just something that we can't afford.
zh: 而这是我们承担不起的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why we need custom models that are more precise.
zh: 这就是为什么我们需要更精确的定制模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Precision matters in our world.
zh: 在我们的世界里，精确性至关重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other thing is, context matters a lot.
zh: 另一件事是，上下文非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you're moving in a design process or you're moving from design to construction, so much information gets lost.
zh: 当你在设计流程中推进，或者从设计转向施工时，大量信息会丢失。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other thing that's really important, and we'll learn this over time, and I think this is going to be the zeitgeist for the next year or two, it's expensive to use a horizontal tool to solve vertical problems.
zh: 还有一点非常重要，我们会随着时间认识到这一点，我认为这会是未来一两年内的时代思潮：用横向工具去解决纵向问题，成本很高。

speaker: Unknown
en: Say more.
zh: 展开说说。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you have a tool that's trained on large amounts of data with a lot of complex interconnections and it has to go through complex cycles and you have to design a series of prompts to get the right answer, you are burning a lot of compute to get there.
zh: 当你有一个用海量数据训练、内部有大量复杂互联关系的工具，它必须经过复杂的循环，而且你必须设计一整套提示词才能得到正确答案，你就是在烧掉大量的算力来达到目的。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, if a tool that's maybe a smaller model that's designed to specifically solve another problem and you don't have to engage in a lot of prompts because the tool already knows what you're trying to accomplish.
zh: 然而，如果一个工具也许是一个更小的模型，专门为解决另一个问题而设计，而且你不必进行大量提示，因为这个工具已经知道你想完成什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: The ability to deliver precision, speed, and total cost of ownership is going to define vertical software in the future with AI.
zh: 在 AI 时代的未来，交付精确性、速度和总拥有成本的能力，将定义纵向软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious in this moment where perhaps the war for top tier talent is more vicious, more competitive, more difficult than it has ever been, especially in Silicon Valley.
zh: 我很好奇，在当下这个争夺顶尖人才的战争比以往任何时候都更激烈、更具竞争性、更困难的时代，尤其是在硅谷——

speaker: Unknown
en: How are you winning?
zh: 你是怎么取胜的？

speaker: Unknown
en: How are you getting people to Autodesk?
zh: 你是怎么把人才吸引到 Autodesk 的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Say you're out in a war and you're fighting a tough battle.
zh: 假设你在战场上，正在打一场艰苦的战斗。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right?
zh: 好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: You're trying to get up the hill, you're under tense enemy attack, and you look behind you and you're hoping your team's behind you.
zh: 你正努力攻上山头，你处在敌人猛烈的攻击之下，你回头望去，希望你的团队跟在你身后。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who do you want behind you?
zh: 你想要谁跟在你身后？

speaker: Unknown
en: The one that believes in your mission or the one that you paid to be there, the mercenary?
zh: 是相信你使命的人，还是你付钱雇来的人，雇佣兵？

speaker: Unknown
en: You want the one who believes in your mission.
zh: 你想要相信你使命的那个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: The mercenary is fickle.
zh: 雇佣兵是善变的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Will change their mind very rapidly on things.
zh: 会在很多事情上很快改变主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I, sorry, I used a war analogy, but it's just helpful.
zh: 好吧，抱歉，我用了一个战争的类比，但它很有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of mercenaries out there.
zh: 外面有很多雇佣兵。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a lot of people that think, I'm so amazing, you know, and I'm worth this $10 million check out of nowhere.
zh: 也有很多人认为，我太了不起了，你知道吗，我值一张凭空出现的 1000 万美元支票。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you know what?
zh: 而你知道吗？

en: Go chase those people.
zh: 去追那些人吧。

en: Go chase them.
zh: 去追他们。

en: Go chase the prima donnas.
zh: 去追那些 prima donnas(自视甚高的明星人物)。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go chase the people that will go to the highest bidder.
zh: 去追那些谁出价高就去谁那儿的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Chase them.
zh: 追他们去吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go at it all day.
zh: 追上一整天都行。

en: I find in my world and at Autodesk, you find the people that love the problem.
zh: 我在我的领域里、在 Autodesk 发现，你要去找那些热爱这个问题的人。

en: Oh God, how many times have I been recruited out of the company?
zh: 天哪，有多少次有人想从公司挖走我？

speaker: Unknown
en: I love what our customers do.
zh: 我热爱我们的客户所做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love the ecosystem.
zh: 我热爱这个生态系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: I go home every night thinking I do something that's useful to the world.
zh: 我每天晚上回家时都在想，我在做一些对世界有用的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't go home thinking I screwed up teenagers' minds.
zh: 我回家时不会想着我毁掉了青少年的心智。

en: I don't go home thinking I screwed up the whole publishing industry.
zh: 我回家时不会想着我毁掉了整个出版业。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't go home with any of those feelings.
zh: 我回家时没有那些感受。

speaker: Unknown
en: I go home feeling like I'm doing something important.
zh: 我回家时感觉自己正在做重要的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll take 10 of those over 100 of those other people.
zh: 这样的人给我 10 个，胜过另外那种人 100 个。

speaker: Unknown
en: That simple.
zh: 就是这么简单。

en: I was at Web Summit Portugal last year and I walked off stage.

en: The question that was asked was, what is the leadership skill that's gonna be most important in this next era?
zh: 当时被问到的问题是，在下一个时代，最重要的领导力技能是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And my reflexive answer, the answer I gave was empathy.
zh: 而我的本能回答，我给出的答案是同理心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

zh: 你谈到同理心，你践行同理心，你有一套核心的领导力信念，其中同理心是核心。

speaker: Unknown
en: How does that manifest?
zh: 这体现在哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you lead that way?
zh: 你是如何以这种方式领导的？

en: Why?
zh: 为什么？

zh: 听着，我认为那些说同理心是弱点的人并不理解同理心。

en: They get a lot of airtime.
zh: 他们获得了很多曝光。

speaker: Unknown
en: They suck a lot of air out of the room because they're successful.
zh: 他们吸走了房间里大量的空气，因为他们很成功。

en: I would argue they're just one trick ahead of their next trick or mistake, but that's another argument for another day.

zh: 听着，我以勇气、学识和同理心为信条行事，好吗？

zh: 而且，你知道，如果你去和销售团队谈，蚕食者无处不在，你知道，他们要来干掉你了，好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: But you rarely encounter them.
zh: 但你很少遇到他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: You also have to have the courage to tell people what they need to hear, not what they wanna hear.
zh: 你还必须有勇气告诉人们他们需要听的话，而不是他们想听的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you also have to have the courage to say, I don't know.
zh: 但你也必须有勇气说：我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the counterbalance of courage, courage without empathy is just meanness and nastiness.
zh: 所以勇气需要制衡，没有同理心的勇气只是刻薄和恶毒。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to know how your courageous act is going to land with particular audiences.
zh: 你必须知道你勇敢的举动会如何影响到特定的受众。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if you want those people behind you and you want them moving with you when the world tacks left or right, and you want them to stick around when things get hard,
zh: 因为如果你想让你背后的那些人，当世界向左或向右转向时你想让他们与你一起行动，当事情变得艰难时你想让他们留下来，

speaker: Unknown
en: You've got to know what their impact is.
zh: 你就必须知道你的举动对他们的影响是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't mean you stop.
zh: 这不意味着你停下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Empathy is not sympathy.
zh: 同理心不是同情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's something very different.
zh: 它是非常不同的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going, I know this is going to hurt for you.
zh: 它是说：我知道这会让你受伤。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I understand that.
zh: 而且我理解这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me tell you why I'm doing it.
zh: 让我告诉你我为什么要这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And let me tell you what I'll do about it in the future.
zh: 让我告诉你我今后会怎么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what empathy is, right?
zh: 这就是同理心，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Empathy is the way you glue courage with an outcome.
zh: 同理心是你把勇气与结果粘合在一起的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think anybody that thinks it's other than that is just confused.
zh: 我认为任何不这么认为的人都只是糊涂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't think you can lead, especially large organizations, without knowing what the ramifications of your actions are.
zh: 而且我认为，如果不了解你行为的后果，你无法领导，尤其是大型组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: My life has taught me.
zh: 我的人生教会了我。

speaker: Unknown
en: That every action you take has a ramification on somebody else.
zh: 你采取的每一个行动都会对别人产生影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you do not understand it, it will blow back on you in some way, or you will cause damage that you do not understand.
zh: 如果你不理解它，它会以某种方式反噬到你身上，或者你会造成你自己都不了解的伤害。

speaker: Unknown
en: You will harm people and you will harm your objectives.
zh: 你会伤害他人，也会伤害你的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think empathy is a superpower.
zh: 所以我认为同理心是一种超能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you have to use it wisely.
zh: 我认为你必须明智地使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't tip into sympathy.
zh: 你不要滑向同情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't let it paralyze you.
zh: 你不要让它让你瘫痪。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reason I glue it together with scholarship is you always have to learn enough to know what you're going into.
zh: 我把它与学识粘合在一起的原因是，你总是必须学习足够多，才能知道你正在进入的是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a wood plaque up in my office.
zh: 我办公室里挂着一块木牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: It says, impulsiveness is not a virtue.
zh: 上面写着：冲动不是美德。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can't believe how many people I've had in my office that try to convince me impulsiveness is a virtue.
zh: 你无法相信有多少人在我办公室里试图说服我冲动是一种美德。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're confusing impulsiveness with boldness or decisiveness.
zh: 而且他们把冲动与大胆或果断混淆了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Impulsiveness is action without thought.
zh: 冲动是不经思考的行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what you want when you're in a terrible, risky situation.
zh: 那是当你处于可怕的危险境地时你想要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your life's in danger.
zh: 你的生命处于危险中。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want muscle memory.
zh: 你想要的是肌肉记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want things moving.
zh: 你要事情在推进。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's where split-second decisions matter.
zh: 这是分秒必争的决策才重要的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you use it for like, you know, oh, you know, I met my wife impulsively and you use it to make a decision and you turn out married to that person for 50 years, you got lucky.
zh: 当你冲动地用它,比如,你知道,哦,你知道,我是冲动之下遇到我妻子的,你用它做了个决定,结果和那个人结婚了 50 年,那是你走运。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, you got lucky, all right?
zh: 哦,你是走运了,好吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And you don't want to play luck on big long-term skills.
zh: 你不想在重大长期的事情上赌运气。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just want to think, do enough scholarship to know what's going on.
zh: 你只需要思考,做足够的功课来了解正在发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't want analysis paralysis because that's what, that's it.
zh: 你不想要分析瘫痪,因为那就是,就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, too much thinking, that's analysis paralysis.
zh: 哦,想太多了,那就是分析瘫痪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, you know, no thinking is stupidity.
zh: 那么,你知道,完全不思考就是愚蠢。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you want to strike the balance.
zh: 所以你要找到平衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why I've always talked about this notion of courage, scholarship, and empathy.
zh: 这就是为什么我一直谈论勇气、学识和同理心这个理念。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I bookmark everything with courage and empathy because I just think you have to lead that way.
zh: 我用勇气和同理心给一切做标记,因为我就是认为你必须以那种方式领导。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, here's to more courage and empathy and scholarship across our world.
zh: 那么,敬我们这个世界更多的勇气、同理心和学识。

speaker: Unknown
en: Lord knows we need it.
zh: 老天知道我们需要这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, in our political system maybe too.
zh: 是啊,在我们的政治体系里也许也需要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, let's go there since you raised it before we wrap up.
zh: 好,既然你提起来了,那我们在收尾前就聊聊这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've been public about your political views and a lot of CEOs are unwilling or too afraid or too concerned to speak up on their beliefs.
zh: 你一直公开表达你的政治观点,而很多 CEO 不愿意、太害怕或者太顾虑而不敢公开表达自己的信念。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why are you public about where you stand?
zh: 你为什么公开表明自己的立场?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I care a lot about this world.
zh: 因为我非常在乎这个世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not beholden to any particular point of view.
zh: 我不受任何特定观点的约束。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been a radical independent most of my life.
zh: 我这辈子大部分时间都是一个激进的独立派。

speaker: Unknown
en: I lean left, obviously.
zh: 我显然偏左。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I'll take an idea from whatever side and I'll run with it if it's a good idea.
zh: 但无论哪个side的好主意,我都会采纳并付诸行动,只要它是个好主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the only way you find out if there's good ideas is that you act reasonably with people.
zh: 但你发现好想法的唯一途径,就是你合理地与人相处。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the how matters a lot in how you lead.
zh: 所以「如何做」在你如何领导这件事上非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't separate the how and the what in leadership.
zh: 在领导中,你无法把「如何做」和「做什么」分开。

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe I don't agree with all the what's that someone says, but I see a how that can get to better what's.
zh: 所以也许我不认同某个人说的所有「做什么」,但我看到一种能够通向更好「做什么」的「如何做」。

speaker: Unknown
en: I pay attention to that because I care about this country.
zh: 我会关注这一点,因为我在乎这个国家。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love this country.
zh: 我爱这个国家。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I'm the product of immigrants.
zh: 你知道,我是移民的产物。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm an immigrant success story in many, many respects.
zh: 在很多很多方面,我都是一个移民成功的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I love the way this country has been able to pull in people from all sorts of places and then refresh itself and refresh itself.
zh: 我喜欢这个国家能够从各种地方吸纳人才,然后一次又一次地自我更新。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we've been in these dark places before.
zh: 而且我们以前也经历过这些黑暗时期。

speaker: Unknown
en: People forget about the 1920s.
zh: 人们忘了 20 世纪 20 年代。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had the postmaster general censoring mail.
zh: 我们有过邮政部长审查邮件的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've had dark worlds in this country and we've always come out of them, but they require people that get the how.
zh: 这个国家经历过黑暗的时代,而我们总是走了出来,但那需要懂得「如何做」的人,

speaker: Unknown
en: of how you bring people together.
zh: 懂得如何把人们团结在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right now, we're shifting into demagoguery on all sides, and that's not gonna get us out of this.
zh: 现在,我们正在滑向各方的煽动蛊惑,而那不会让我们走出困境。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I speak up because, not because I might speak up on a particular issue or something, I speak up because I care about how things get done.
zh: 所以我公开发声,不是因为我可能会就某个特定议题发声,我发声是因为我在乎事情是如何办成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if we don't do things right, we thrash.
zh: 因为如果我们不把事情做对,我们就会陷入混乱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we thrash, we lose.
zh: 而如果我们陷入混乱,我们就会输。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm so grateful for you.
zh: 我非常感激你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for being on Masters of Scale.
zh: 谢谢你来到《Masters of Scale》。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, it was a pleasure.
zh: 哦,这是我的荣幸。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks, Jeff.
zh: 谢谢,Jeff。

speaker: Unknown
en: This has been great.
zh: 这真是太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks again to Andrew Anagnost for joining us on Masters of Scale.
zh: 再次感谢 Andrew Anagnost 来到《Masters of Scale》。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is so much of this conversation that will stick with me, but perhaps the most important lesson Andrew shared is the one that he learned as a teenager.
zh: 这场对话中有很多内容会一直留在我心里,但 Andrew 分享的最重要的经验,也许是他十几岁时学到的那一条。

speaker: Unknown
en: You benefit most from surrounding yourself with people who tell you what you need to hear, not what you want to hear.
zh: 让身边围绕那些告诉你需要听什么、而不是你想听什么的人,你会受益最多。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you can hear the people saying the hard things, the possibilities are endless.
zh: 如果你能听进那些说难听话的人,可能性就是无限的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Jeff Berman.
zh: 我是 Jeff Berman。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for listening.
zh: 感谢您的收听。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, listeners.
zh: 嘿，各位听众。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bob here.
zh: 我是 Bob。

zh: 如果您在 Masters of Scale 上收听 Rapid Response,您可能错过了节目的一半，因为每周五我们会在 Rapid Response 订阅源中独家发布第二期 Rapid Response。

en: The guests and topics are just as compelling and timely from Ford's CEO to NASA's administrator to the lessons from the Devil Wears Prada.
zh: 嘉宾和话题同样引人入胜且紧扣时事，从福特 CEO 到 NASA 局长，再到《穿普拉达的女王》带来的启示。

en: It takes about 10 seconds to find.
zh: 找到它只需大约 10 秒钟。

zh: 只需在您收听播客的任意平台搜索 Rapid Response 并点击关注，确保您不错过任何一集。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope to see you there.
zh: 希望在那里见到您。

zh: Masters of Scale 是 Wait What 的原创节目。

zh: 混音与母带处理由音频 boys,Aaron Bestinelli 和 Brian Pugh 完成。

zh: 访问 mastersofscale.com 查找本集的文字稿并订阅我们的简报。
